bilingual.notes: Bilingual Education Extension: add-on only, attached to a valid base certificate. Approved program requires coursework in six content areas, ≥50 clock hours of college-supervised field experience, and the Bilingual Education Assessment (BEA), which doubles as the language-proficiency instrument for the language other than English.

eld.notes: Branded ESOL in OTI certification listings and TESOL in higher-ed program names. Standalone classroom-teacher certificate (CST 116 ESOL) plus supplementary pathway for already-certified teachers. Programs (Fall 2024+) require ≥100 clock hours of field experience and ≥70 school days of student teaching with ELL students. 12 LOTE semester hours required as coursework precondition but not as a target-language proficiency demonstration.

sei.notes: No universal SEI/EL credential mandate. CR Part 154 requires general classroom teachers of ELLs to dedicate 15% of CTLE clock hours to language acquisition addressing the needs of ELLs — a continuing-education obligation, not a credential mandate.

history.title: Aspira v. Board of Education of the City of New York consent decree (S.D.N.Y.)
history.description: ASPIRA of New York and Puerto Rican parents settled their 1972 class action against the New York City Board of Education with a consent decree that became the country's first court-ordered bilingual-education program of any scale. The decree required NYC to identify Spanish-speaking ELs and provide a Transitional Bilingual Education program (Spanish-language content instruction plus intensive ESL) for any student whose ability to participate effectively in English was below grade level. Aspira's compliance regime was the operational model that NYSED later codified for the state in CR Part 154 and remains the doctrinal touchstone for NYC's bilingual-extension teacher demand.

history.title: NYSESLAT introduced as the state ELP assessment
history.description: New York adopted the New York State English as a Second Language Achievement Test (NYSESLAT) as its annual ELP assessment in 2003. NY has never been a WIDA Consortium member; the companion identification screener is NYSITELL. Coded as elpAssessment.consortium=null because NYSESLAT is state-specific.

history.title: New York State Seal of Biliteracy enacted
history.description: Chapter 416 of the Laws of 2012 (signed 2012-12-17) authorized the New York State Seal of Biliteracy (NYSSB) administered by NYSED's Office of Bilingual Education and World Languages. First seals issued 2013-14. Coded as sealOfBiliteracy.year=2013 to reflect the first-award year.

history.title: CR Part 154 Multilingual Learner / ELL regulations adopted
history.description: Board of Regents adopted revised Commissioner's Regulations Part 154 (Sept. 2014, effective school year 2015-16) governing services for ELLs/MLs, including the requirement that general classroom teachers of ELLs dedicate 15% of CTLE clock hours to language acquisition. CR Part 154 (not a new credential) is the operative ELL service mandate; underpins the sei notes.
